findings.title: Access check enhancements to prevent unauthorized disclosure of file paths (KB5058189)
findings.summary_md: Microsoft documents a Windows vulnerability, referenced as CVE-2025-21197 and CVE-2025-27738, where a user with FILE_LIST_DIRECTORY rights on a parent folder obtains directory change notifications revealing full paths of files they cannot access. A fix shipped in Windows updates on or after April 8, 2025, performing a FILE_LIST_DIRECTORY access check before reporting changes. The fix is disabled by default and must be enabled via the EnforceDirectoryChangeNotificationPermissionCheck registry or group policy value under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Policies or Control\FileSystem.

findings.title: fsnotify: do not generate ACCESS/MODIFY events on child for special files
findings.summary_md: Mainline Linux commit 635bc4def026 by Amir Goldstein, committed by Jan Kara on December 15, 2025, stops fsnotify from delivering ACCESS/MODIFY events to parent-directory watchers for special files such as those under /dev, closing the keystroke-timing side channel. Reported by Sudheendra Raghav Neela of TU Graz, marked for stable, and the commit message cites the researchers' paper PDF. The description notes events are still generated to parent watchers via utimensat(), so the mitigation is partial.

findings.title: CVE-2025-68788 detail (NVD record)
findings.summary_md: The NVD record for CVE-2025-68788, published January 13, 2026 with kernel.org as source, describes the fsnotify behavior allowing a user with no read access to a file but read access to its parent directory to observe access/modify events, aligned with stat-based atime/mtime semantics. It lists fix commits and shows affected Linux ranges with stable branches unaffected from 5.10.248, 5.15.198, and 6.1.160 onward. Siemens additionally flags the SIMATIC S7-1500 CPU 1518-4 PN/DP MFP at V3.1.6 and earlier as affected.
